input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: § 12.4 (p0046) binds the Customer, not the Vendor, and imposes a post-term non-compete of 24 months with undefined scope ("any product or service that competes with Vendor") and unlimited territory, with no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions. That is walk-away territory under the rule and fails the fallback on every material term (scope, duration, term-only limitation, carve-outs). It also directly contradicts § 12.3 (p0044), where Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no non-compete commitment. The minimal fix is deletion of p0046, which restores the preferred position and removes the internal inconsistency. The separate no-hire restriction at p0045 is left to its own rule.

proposal.summary: Delete the non-compete restriction on Customer in § 12.4
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept restrictions on the businesses we operate or the products we develop, buy or sell, so we have deleted this non-compete; it also directly contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no non-compete commitment. If the relationship needs protection, we could consider a restriction limited to a single named competing product, during the term only and capped at 12 months, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
